en: Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*anāsava*) and not associated with a root (*ahetuka*), a state that is without conflict and associated with a root arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict and not associated with a root, a state that is with conflict (*sāsava*) and associated with a root arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are two; ... pe ... in the case of the prenascence and repetition conditions, there is one; ... pe ... in the case of the resultant condition, there is one; ... pe ... in the case of the non-disappearance condition, there are two.

Dependent on a state that is neither-conflict (na-araṇa) and not dissociated from the root (na-hetu-vippayutta), a state that is conflict-free (araṇa) and dissociated from the root arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not-conflict (na-araṇa) and not dissociated from the root, a state that is conflict-free and dissociated from the root [arises].
[It] arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Two [types of conditions] in the case of the root; one in the case of the object … pe … four in the case of conascence … pe … one in the case of result … pe … four in the case of non-disappearance.
